events.title: Grant Wins at Fort Donelson
events.description: After a hard-fought battle in Tennessee, Union forces under General Ulysses S. Grant captured Fort Donelson. Grant demanded that the Confederate garrison surrender unconditionally, and he got it.
events.significance: It was one of the Union's first major victories of the American Civil War. It opened the Cumberland River to Union forces and made Grant a national figure. Newspapers nicknamed him "Unconditional Surrender" Grant.

events.title: Lithuania Declares Independence
events.description: In Vilnius, the Council of Lithuania signed the Act of Independence. It proclaimed the restoration of an independent Lithuanian state, even though German troops still occupied the country.
events.significance: The act laid the foundation for modern Lithuania. February 16 is still celebrated there as Statehood Day.

events.title: Howard Carter Opens Tutankhamun's Burial Chamber
events.description: British archaeologist Howard Carter unsealed the burial chamber of the pharaoh Tutankhamun in Egypt's Valley of the Kings. Inside he found the king's sarcophagus, which had been sealed for more than 3,000 years. Some sources record the unsealing as taking place on February 17.
events.significance: The discovery of the nearly intact royal tomb set off worldwide fascination with ancient Egypt. It remains one of the most celebrated finds in the history of archaeology.

events.title: Fidel Castro Sworn In as Premier of Cuba
events.description: Weeks after the Cuban Revolution overthrew dictator Fulgencio Batista, Fidel Castro took the oath as Cuba's premier in Havana.
events.significance: Castro went on to lead Cuba for nearly five decades. His rule reshaped Cuban society and made the island a central player in Cold War tensions.
